memory_candidates.content: When a Claude Code dispatch needs to join back to its own transcript, the exact-match key is the dispatch prompt's own embedded Context JSON block (task_number + dispatch_seq) read from the FIRST line's .message.content as a plain string -- read it with `jq -r '.message.content'` (never raw-grep the still-escaped line) and anchor the match so e.g. 330 does not match 3300. Transcripts live at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<cc_session_id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl where <slug> replaces every non-alphanumeric character in the absolute repo root with '-'. Nearest-timestamp or .meta.json description matching are both unreliable across re-dispatches of the same task+phase.

A git-log --grep subject-convention commit selector (e.g. matching 'task N: ...' / 'task N phase P: ...') is NOT safe against task-number reuse after a vault/archive operation renumbers tasks: an unfiltered match can silently pull in an unrelated historical task's commits that happened to reuse the same number years earlier, corrupting any derived delta (e.g. a wall-clock computed between two matched commits that are not actually adjacent in the same task's lifecycle). When building a --backfill-style derivation over commit history, either scope the git log to a recency/date window or filter the output to the task's actual lifetime before trusting cross-commit deltas.
